answers.answer: Follow the five steps under Hear your first spoken reply. 1: on the OBS page, choose Overlays in OBS and find TTS caption in Required overlays. 2: choose Connect, add it in the OBS app as a Browser source using the dialog's settings, and keep Control audio via OBS on. 3: open Text to speech, then Rules. Check that Read messages aloud is on, Moderators approve first is off, Who may be heard is Everyone and Minimum bits is 0. 4: choose a voice on Voices and play its sample. 5: on a chat command, enable Read it aloud, save it and run the command in chat. To choose who is heard, set Who may be heard in the Speaking panel on the Rules tab. Every step can be done as written and no action is missing.
answers.quote: Choose Connect. In the OBS app, add it as a Browser source using the dialog’s settings. Keep Control audio via OBS on.

answers.answer: You need one of the roles that may change the settings. An Editor role is needed to switch a reward on in Rewards that speak. You also need the TTS caption browser source in OBS and something that requests speech, such as a command, reward, event response or pipeline. Both are stated near the top of the page and under Who can use this page.
answers.quote: A Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster may open the page and change the settings.

answers.answer: Success is hearing the reply through OBS and seeing the caption. The voice sample in the dashboard only checks the voice. Running the command checks the whole path to the stream. The Spoken history row does not prove that a line played, because the row is saved before the line reaches OBS.
answers.quote: You should hear the reply through OBS and see the caption when the source displays it.

answers.answer: To limit ordinary viewers, set Who may be heard to Moderators in Speaking on the Rules tab. This setting checks the role of the person whose own words are read. Command replies count as Everyone with 0 bits, so they stop being read and cannot be used for the moderators' test. The built-in Rewards that speak path bypasses Who may be heard, so any reward that is switched on still reads ordinary viewers. To keep viewers out, leave rewards off (switching one on needs Editor). To fix a pronunciation, use Pronunciation, then Add rule, and fill in Phrase and Say instead (and Exact sound (IPA) for Azure). Use the row's play button to hear it. For the channel name, use How to say the channel name on Keys, then Preview and Save spelling.
answers.quote: So for a command reply, any Who may be heard above Everyone, or any Minimum bits above 0, stops that reply from being read.

answers.answer: I reread to learn that the reward path ignores Who may be heard. This only appears after the role setting is explained, so a streamer who raised the role to keep viewers out would still hear viewer rewards. The cost is one reread. The page does state it before the Rewards that speak setup, so it is not a blocking gap.
answers.quote: Who may be heard, Minimum bits and Cooldown are bypassed when the reward’s built-in Rewards that speak path reads its submitted text.
